Article Title: ‘Everyone stands to learn from his experiences’: PM Modi releases former President Ram Nath Kovind’s autobiography
Article Text:
Former President Ram Nath Kovind with PM Narendra Modi at book launch

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday released the autobiography of former President Ram Nath Kovind and urged the “new generation” to draw lessons from Kovind’s writings and experiences.The book, "The Times of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles," was released at an event in the national capital in the presence of the former president.“Learn about Kovind ji’s life journey in his own words. Let the new generation of the country read his writings and his experiences; everyone stands to learn a great deal from them,” PM Modi said, describing the book’s title as “very apt”.Explaining the title, he added, “The underlying message is that while his life and the struggles within it were personal, the triumph achieved as a result of those struggles belongs to the Indian Republic—to India’s democracy.”
Article Summary: The book, "The Times of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles," was released at an event in the national capital in the presence of the former president. “Learn about Kovind ji’s life journey in his own words,” PM Modi said.

Article Title: ‘Bharat is one, and will be forever’: VP Radhakrishnan flags off Tiranga bike rally in Delhi, NDA MPs participate
Article Text:
NDA MPs participate in 'Tiranga Yatra' rally in Delhi

NEW DELHI: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan on Wednesday flagged off a “Har Ghar Tiranga” bike rally in the national capital ahead of Independence Day celebrations on August 15.The rally, organised as part of the ongoing “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign, saw participation from MPs of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and a large number of supporters carrying the national flag. The rally is scheduled to cover the stretch from Bharat Mandapam to Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium.Addressing participants, Radhakrishnan noted that the various activities organised under the campaign may differ in form but carry the same sentiment of national belonging.“In Tiranga Yatra, bike rallies, cultural programmes, the activities are different but the sentiment they carry is the same, that is the collective sense of belonging... I urge each one of you to actively engage in this campaign and inspire every citizen to hoist the Tricolour with pride,” ANI quoted him as saying.The vice president also emphasised the unity of the country, declaring, “Bharat is one, and it will be one forever.”He paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya, who designed the national flag, and recalled Hansa Mehta, who led a group of 72 women who presented the first National Flag of independent India to Dr Rajendra Prasad, the country’s first president.Several NDA MPs attended the rally. BJP MP Tarun Chugh highlighted the enthusiasm of young people and their resolve to contribute towards the goal of a developed India.“Under the leadership of PM Modi, the youth have come out today with the resolution of ‘Viksit Bharat’. Tiranga is the pride of India. Under PM Modi, India will realise the resolve to become a developed India,” Chugh said.Union minister of state for Home Nityanand Rai highlighted the significance of the national flag, describing the Tricolour as a sentiment deeply connected with the country and its people.“The Tiranga is our pride, and it is more precious to us than our life,” Rai said.BJP MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri pointed to the participation of a large number of MPs in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for the Tiranga Yatra.“In response to PM Modi's call, a large number of MPs are joining this Tiranga Yatra today, and the Vice President will inaugurate this Tiranga Yatra. The journey will go from Bharat Mandapam to the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, and a spectacular celebration is visible here,” Bidhuri said.The “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign is being held across the country ahead of Independence Day, encouraging citizens, public representatives and organisations to display the national flag.The Delhi rally is part of a series of programmes being organised in the capital to mark Independence Day, with the Tricolour at the centre of celebrations aimed at strengthening the sense of unity and national pride.
Article Summary: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan flagged off a 'Har Ghar Tiranga' bike rally in Delhi. The rally saw participation from MPs of the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and a large number of supporters carrying the national flag. The Delhi rally is part of a series of programmes being organised in the capital to mark Independence Day.

Article Title: Medical device industry seeks rethink of draft law, urges separate regulatory body
Article Text:
The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Representative Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the Draft Drugs, Medical Devices & Cosmetics Bill, 2026."The Bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for India's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally", an industry expert told TOI.The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to ensure their quality, safety and efficacy.In a letter to govt, the associations say that the draft bill, in its current form, treats medical devices as an adjunct to pharmaceuticals, despite clear scientific, engineering, and regulatory distinction between the two.Medical devices are engineering products, and should not be clubbed with pharmaceuticals, the letter says, adding the draft Bill continues to use drug-centric terminology such as "adulterated", "spurious"."misbranded", and applies pharma-style criminalisation to engineering deviations.Globally, medical devices are regulated through risk-based conformity assessment and quality management systems.Further, the Bill does not provide for a dedicated regulatory authority for medical devices, despite repeated recommendations.In 2023, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry argued that proposed overarching legislation (such as the Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics draft) fails the domestic sector by continuing to regulate medical devices as "drugs" under a joint framework, instead of establishing an independent, specialized regulatory body.Administrative enforcement including recalls, corrective actions, civil penalties-- should replace imprisonment for technical lapses, the letter by 11 associations including Aimed, AHPI (Association of Healthcare Providers India), ADMI (Association of Diagnostics Manufacturers) and Patient Safety and Access Initiative, says.The Bill 2026 applies uniform penalties across all device classes, from low-risk surgical instruments to high-risk implants, contrary to global norms.It does not clearly recognise key medical device standards covering areas such as biocompatibility, usability and software safety.While the draft has been circulated to various ministries and departments, key stakeholders, including industry associations, manufacturers and hospital bodies, have not been adequately involved in the process, the industry executive said, adding it appears inconsistent with the pre-legislative consultation process.
Article Summary: The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. It would consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics. The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the draft.

Article Title: 'Generation gutter' remark on NEET protesters: Agra lawyer files case against BJP MP Kangana Ranaut

NEW DELHI: An Agra-based lawyer on Wednesday said he has filed a case against BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut over her remarks describing students who protested against the NEET paper leak as “Generation gutter.”Rajiv Gandhi Bar Association president and advocate Ramashankar Sharma alleged that Ranaut had “insulted” the students and their parents. He also accused the BJP MP of having a “habit” of making such remarks."I have filed a suit in the Special Court for MPs/MLAs. The suit concerns Kangana Ranaut referring to students protesting at Jantar Mantar as the 'gutter generation'. She has a habit of making such remarks. She has insulted the country's students and abused their parents... This is a matter concerning the students' future," Sharma told ANI.The court is scheduled to hear the matter on August 21.The case comes after Ranaut criticised students protesting over the NEET paper leak, describing some of them as “Generation Gutter” and questioning their behaviour and language.In a series of posts on Instagram Stories, the actor-politician described videos from the agitation as “puke-inducing” and criticised the protesters for what she called their “crass” language and behaviour.She also questioned the "upbringing" of the young protesters and criticised some young women for trying to emulate independent career women without “earning that freedom”.Ranaut later wrote that some protesters had “nothing to offer to the system” and were “not good at studies”, referring to them as “Generation Gutter”.The agitation was called off on July 25 after then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. During the agitation, some youngsters allegedly abused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother.They were booked after the protests ended, following which PM Modi said he had "forgiven" the alleged abusers.

Article Title: 'Much more to this than meets the eye': Rahul targets PM Modi after US court drops case against Adani
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani 's acquittal by a US court and targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development.In a post on X, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said, "There is much more to this than meets the eye. A compromised PM was forced to sell India’s interest. India is paying a huge price. "A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two-year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused. The US Department of Justice had sought dismissal of the charges, citing six “overlapping bases”, including that the case involved foreign conduct, India had not found “actionable misconduct”, no money had been lost on securities issued and there were “extraordinary proof problems”.The case, filed in November 2024, accused Adani, his nephew Sagar Adani and six others of conspiracy to bribe Indian government officials to secure a solar power contract. The Adani Group had denied the allegations and said its companies and executives had acted in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.Judge Nicholas Garaufis had earlier questioned the DOJ's decision to drop the case and sought further explanation for the move.The DOJ had argued that the defendants were foreign nationals who had never appeared in the US and were unlikely to do so.Adani, meanwhile, welcomed the court's decision, saying: “Throughout this challenging period, our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering. My deepest gratitude to those who never lost faith in us, in the system and in India’s capacity for justice,” according to the supplied text.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday reacted sharply to Gautam Adani's acquittal by a US court. He targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development. A US federal judge in New York on Monday dismissed the nearly two- year-old criminal case against Adani and the other accused.

Article Title: Parl Panel flags shortfall in achieving even 25% of skill development targets under action plan for persons with disabilities
Article Text:
​Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities

NEW DELHI: The parliamentary standing committee on social justice and empowerment has brought into focus the failure of the National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities (NAP-SDP) to meet setout targets and highlighted that the continued shortfall in achieving even 25% of the set targets is a matter of serious concern.The panel in its latest report tabled in Parliament on Monday yet again raised the issue which it had flagged in its earlier report in March saying that the performance of the action plan remained significantly below the set targets over the last three years.In the report on the action taken by the government on the observations and recommendations made in March on ‘Demands for Grants (2026-27)’ of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the panel said that it has not accepted the reply of the govt on NAP-SDP and added that it requires reiteration.The Committee, in its original report, had observed with concern that under the (NAP-SDP) the performance data reveals a widening gap. Against a target of 17,000 in 2023–24, the Department trained 9,333 beneficiaries; this fell sharply to 836 trainees against a target of 15,000 in 2024–25. Though higher than the previous year in 2025-2026 as of January 2,264 beneficiaries were trained against a target of 10,000.The panel chaired by BJP MP in Lok Sabha PC while acknowledging the administrative challenges posed by the transition to the PM DAKSH-DEPwD portal and the Hybrid Treasury Single Account (TSA) model, had said that the continued shortfall in achieving even 25% of the set targets was cited as a matter of serious concern.With the newly announced Divyangjan Kaushal Yojana, the Committee recommended that the Department adopt a more robust, industry-linked approach to bridge the gap between training and gainful employment. “It is essential that the Department prioritize the placement of certified trainees by strengthening partnerships with private employers and ensuring that training modules remain aligned with current market demands,” the committee had recommended.The Committee had further suggested that the targets for the 2026–27 fiscal year be monitored quarterly to ensure that the transition to the new Yojana results in a measurable improvement in both the number of beneficiaries trained and their subsequent placement in sustainable employment.The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities in its reply to the Commission dated June 18 said that “the recommendations of the Committee have been noted”. “The new skilling scheme is being designed to address diverse skilling needs and aspirations of all types of Persons with Disabilities, through industry-linked and outcome-based livelihood models. The Department envisages to regularly monitor and review the scheme. ”
Article Summary: Parliamentary standing committee on social justice and empowerment has brought into focus the failure of the National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities (NAP-SDP) to meet setout targets. The panel in its latest report tabled in Parliament on Monday yet again raised the issue which it had flagged in its earlier report.

Article Title: 'Images disturb me deeply': Congress's Sam Pitroda questions 'use of force' against Jharkhand students
Article Text:
Sam Pitroda backs Jharkhand student protests

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sam Pitroda on Monday backed protesting students in Jharkhand as an agitation over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations intensified in Ranchi. Criticising the government’s use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons, Pitroda called for “reform, accountability and compassion” as the protests entered their 18th day.The development comes as the Jharkhand students’ 'Vidhan Sabha gherao' march in Ranchi on Monday saw police use lathis and water cannons to disperse protesters. The march was organised over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The protesters are demanding, among other measures, the cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.In a series of posts on X, the Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) global chairman said the grievances of young people should be addressed through dialogue."The images from Ranchi disturb me deeply”, he wrote.Pitroda said students should not be met with force, calling them India's future and expressing solidarity with Jharkhand's youth.In another post, Pitroda said, "Democracy requires governments to create space for peaceful dissent, dialogue and resolution."Pitroda's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students, urging the Jharkhand government to address their grievances. The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government is run by a JMM-led coalition in which the Congress is a partner.Pitroda also said the protesting youth deserved to be heard respectfully and urged authorities to address their concerns over fair examinations, transparent recruitment, employment opportunities and their prospects for the future."These are not unreasonable demands. India owes its youth a system they can trust”, he added in the postHe further said the concerns of students needed to be viewed in the context of the sacrifices made by their families."Behind every protesting student is a family that has sacrificed - often for years for education and the hope of a job.Pitroda criticised the JMM-led Jharkhand government over the handling of recruitment and examination-related grievances, saying delays in recruitment and failures in examinations risk eroding young people's trust in the system. He called for "reform, accountability and compassion" in addressing their concerns.Calling India's youth its "greatest assets", Pitroda said the country's demographic dividend could turn into frustration if education does not translate into opportunities and examinations fail to inspire confidence."We must redesign education, assessment and employment systems for this generation — not punish them for demanding change," he said.On Monday, police and protesters clashed during the march outside the Jharkhand Assembly. Police resorted to at least three rounds of lathicharge, while tear gas shells and water cannons were also used to disperse demonstrators.Injured protester alleged that police began the lathicharge without warning.The police have, however, given a different account of the events. Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said a stone was thrown at a police jawan and alleged that some "anti-social elements" attempted to provoke police and officials during the protest.Addressing a press conference, Bhajantri said the police had exercised restraint throughout the demonstration and used "mild force" only after a situation arose in which a jawan's life was allegedly at risk.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said most students were peaceful but alleged that a section of protesters damaged barricades and pelted stones.The protest also affected Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi after taking part in the march.Mahto had been on hunger strike for nine days at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium before joining the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march despite his deteriorating health. He was later admitted to hospital.The police action drew criticism from political leaders across party lines. On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong. Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X, on Monday.He further urged the Jharkhand government to address the students' grievances."The Jharkhand government must continue to hear these students out and resolve their issues immediately," he added.The JPSC and JSSC examinations have been at the centre of protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has registered an Enforcement Case Information Report under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sam Pitroda criticises government's use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons as protests enter 18th day. Protesters are demanding cancellation of JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages, seeking to address the "neglect of rural educational infrastructure".The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to work together to improve basic facilities in government schools.Dipke said he would launch the initiative from his village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, by approaching the village head and requesting him to take steps to improve government schools there.“The coming 15th August is our 80th Independence Day. But, if anything has been neglected or ignored the most in the last 80 years, it is the government schools in our villages,” Dipke said on Monday.“We have made a new Parliament, a new PM house. Why have we not been able to build new schools in our villages? Do we not consider the children of farmers and labourers the future of our country?” he asked.Dipke said children in villages continue to face difficulties in accessing schools and basic facilities such as drinking water and toilets.“Even today, village children have to walk a long distance to go to school. After going there, they don’t find water or toilet facilities,” he said, highlighting the difficulties faced by girls in particular.“I feel that on this 15th August, if we should pay attention to anything, if we should make a new start, we should start by improving our government schools,” he said.As part of the campaign, the CJP has appealed to sarpanches across the country to take up the task of improving government schools in their respective villages.Dipke said he would personally approach the village head in Hingoli and urged other sarpanches to do the same in their villages.The organisation has termed the initiative the “Sarpanch Challenge”, under which it plans to publicly recognise village heads who improve their schools by sharing before-and-after photographs on its social media platforms and giving credit to the sarpanches concerned.“We will give you credit so that after seeing you, after seeing the schools that you have improved, many other village heads also start improving schools in their villages," Dipke said.The CJP has also called for a citizen-led social audit of government schools.Parents whose children study in government schools have been asked to visit the institutions and check basic facilities, including electricity, clean drinking water, functional washrooms and mid-day meals.“You go to your children's schools and see if basic facilities are available. See if there is electricity, water… Do your children get washroom facilities? Do they get mid-day meals?” Dipke said.He urged parents to record videos if basic facilities were unavailable. The CJP said it would soon issue a printable audit form through which citizens could record the facilities available at their children's schools and those that were missing.The form will be shared through links on campaign videos on the CJP's official social media platforms and completed forms and video evidence can be emailed to the organisation.The campaign aims to ensure that children of farmers and wage labourers studying in village schools have access to facilities comparable to those available to children in cities.“If not, you make videos of it. Because your children's schooling should be good. That is your fundamental right," Dipke said.“Let us all make a promise to the children who live in villages that we will improve their schools. Together, we can do this,” he said, concluding his video with the message, “Real India lives in villages”.In a separate video, Dipke also extended his support to Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was hospitalised after his health deteriorated during a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.Calling the alleged police action against protesters “cruel and inhuman”, Dipke drew a parallel with student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. “Be it Jantar Mantar or Jharkhand, such police brutality against students is cruel and inhuman,” he said.“CJP stands firmly with Devendra bhai and his struggle. He is a true hero. We salute his courage and strength!” he added.Mahto has been at the centre of the ongoing JPSC-JSSC agitation in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike and joined the students' Vidhan Sabha gherao march on Monday, arriving at the protest in an ambulance as his health deteriorated.The CJP, which began as an online satirical platform, later took its campaign to the streets. Its 36-day agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against examination irregularities was called off on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages. The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to improve basic facilities in government schools.

Article Title: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
Article Text:
Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.

NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected."We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said."We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.
Article Summary: Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected. In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries.

Article Title: India move will muddle border talks: China
Article Text:
State-run Global Times quoted Chinese experts as saying India’s move would not alter the legal status of the disputed territory but could complicate future boundary negotiations.

GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation."India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.
Article Summary: India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument. China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh. State-run Global Times claims these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region.

NEW DELHI: The number of govt elementary schools across the country fell by nearly 10,000 in a year, with Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recording the steepest declines, according to data tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday.UDISE+ data showed that the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26 - a reduction of 9,866 schools, or about 1.1%.The govt data was provided in response to a question from DMK MP T R Baalu on whether a large number of elementary schools had been closed because of insufficient student strength and the steps being taken to prevent dropouts. However, the education ministry did not specify how many of the schools were actually closed due to lack of students, while furnishing the overall number of govt elementary schools in the two academic years.Meghalaya recorded the biggest numerical decline, with the number of govt elementary schools falling from 7,633 to 5,459, a drop of 2,174. Telangana followed with a reduction of 1,961 schools, from 22,983 to 21,022, while Andhra Pradesh saw its count decline by 1,446, from 37,449 to 36,003.Madhya Pradesh had 1,043 fewer schools, Karnataka 615, West Bengal 587, Rajasthan 473 and Maharashtra 357. Himachal Pradesh recorded a decline of 259 schools, while Assam had 209 fewer.Uttar Pradesh, which continues to have the largest network of govt elementary schools, saw the number fall marginally from 1,34,115 to 1,33,948.Not every state recorded a decline. Bihar's count rose from 66,803 to 66,915, while Chhattisgarh increased from 43,836 to 43,853. The numbers remained unchanged in Jammu & Kashmir, Puducherry and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.The ministry said opening, closing and rationalisation of schools fall within the jurisdiction of state and UT govts since education is on the Concurrent List.At the same time, it said access to schooling had improved. The Gross Access Ratio rose between 2018-19 and 2025-26 from 96.49 to 98.14 at upper-primary level, from 88.24 to 95.05 at secondary level and from 65.05 to 94.79 at higher-secondary level.The Centre said states were being supported through Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN, besides assistance for school infrastructure, residential schools and hostels, transport facilities, enrolment drives, textbooks and uniforms to curb dropouts and improve enrolment.
Article Summary: Number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26. Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recorded the steepest declines.

Article Title: Phuket-Delhi Air India pilot fails 2nd dope test, was high on marijuana
Article Text:
Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances.

Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into ‘negative G’ situation

What happened on board

What govt is doing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What it means for AI

NEW DELHI: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight after it emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. Besides, the cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high” PIC’s onboard behaviour.The pilot also faces criminal action beyond DGCA rules — which require such a pilot to be sent for de-addiction and allow him to resume flying after being certified drug-free.The young co-pilot had to single-handedly steady the aircraft and then land it safely at the destination.An alarmed civil aviation ministry summoned AI’s outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson to express concern about this incident and find out how the airline was dealing with the issue and review its plan to come out of its prolonged period of operational turbulence.The incident that has raised questions over the robustness of the Indian system has also pushed DGCA to explore ways to make dope test rules more stringent after the incident that left 20 passengers and four cabin crew members injured.“Certain records, statements, medical information and other material collected during the investigation are protected and confidential in accordance with the applicable investigation framework….AAIB (Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau) requests all concerned to respect the investigation process and refrain from drawing conclusions… AAIB will conduct a thorough investigation covering all material facts and relevant evidence and will issue its preliminary findings,” the aviation ministry said in a statement while responding to queries on the confirmatory test.Multiple sources told TOI that the PIC was acting under the influence of psychoactive substances. “He was often sitting on the floor of the flight deck and tried to smoke out. Cabin crew had to help him back to his seat. He was not in full control of himself. He was unable to walk properly after exiting the aircraft,” said a person in the know. AI did not comment on the cabin crew’s alleged complaints.The probe will determine whether the aircraft had a sudden loss of altitude due to a series of multiple and rare technical snags, which have been reported by the co-pilot in his report, or it was caused by actions of the PIC.When the aircraft experienced loss of altitude, the PIC is learnt to have been standing and leaning behind the co-pilot’s seat. The Airbus A320 had momentarily gone into a “negative G” situation when the PIC and things in the cockpit floated up and those who were not wearing seat belts got injured in the passenger cabin.Also read: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government The cabin crew have given a report to AI. The co-pilot may have informed the airline’s ground control about the pilot’s behaviour due to which the unusual step of subjecting the cockpit crew to a drug test — instead of just breath analyser tests — was taken.“AAIB is engaged in systematic collection, preservation and examination of all relevant technical, operational, medical and human-factor evidence,” the govt said.While DGCA is reviewing its rule titled “procedure for examination of aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances”, India’s senior-most pilots sought a differentiation between a pilot testing positive after having a medication for sleeping or anxiety and those who are found to have consumed “true” psychoactive substances.Airlines have a list of medicines that need to be avoided some hours before flight as they can cause drowsiness.Massive financial losses apart, the airline’s operations and training are again under a cloud, just when it was trying to regain public faith following the Ahmedabad crash in June 2025.While Tatas and partner Singapore Airlines have pumped in thousands of crores and there have been significant cosmetic improvements, it is still looking for leadership and professional management that can usher in the culture required to fly it out of turbulence.
Article Summary: Trouble mounted for the pilot-in-command (PIC) of last Tuesday’s badly rattled Phuket-Delhi Air India flight. It emerged that he had failed the confirmatory dope test and was found to have consumed marijuana. The cabin crew of the flight, AI 2379, has filed a complaint with the airline against the “high’ PIC's onboard behaviour.

Article Title: ‘CJP twisted CJI remark’: Supreme Court seeks government, CBI response on PIL
Article Text:
The petitioner said that post-May 15, there has been a quantum increase in clips of selectively edited judicial proceedings.

NEW DELHI: Three months after CJI Surya Kant's 'cockroach' remark sparked a storm and gave birth to Cockroach Janta Party that led a Gen Z protest against NEET-UG paper leak, Supreme Court Tuesday sought responses from govt and CBI on a PIL seeking action against those who commercially exploited the remark through clever editing of virtual court proceedings and draped it with a meaning that was never intended.During a half-an-hour long debate on the issue before a bench comprising CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, petitioner-cum-advocate Raja Choudhary said it requires a deeper investigation as to how the word 'cockroach', used in a completely different context during judicial proceedings on May 15, was selectively picked, cleverly edited and commercially exploited to undermine judicial dignity and hurt institutional integrity. The petitioner sought a direction to authorities "to examine and take action in accordance with law against persons/entities allegedly involved in commercial exploitation, trademark appropriation, monetized circulation, or unauthorised commercial use of oral courtroom observations/metaphors, including activities of CJP, while recognising that fair criticism, democratic dissent, satire, and free speech remain permissible within the constitutional framework without undermining institutional dignity".Referring to the May 15 hearing before a CJI-led bench on a petition 'Sanjay Dubey Vs Registrar General of Delhi HC', Choudhary emphasised the CJI had made the "cockroach" remark in the specific context of fake advocates, as he expressed "concerns regarding misuse of court process, deterioration of professional standards and how it impacted the institution itself".He said post-May 15, there has been a quantum increase in clips of selectively edited judicial proceedings. The distorted versions and oral observations made during court proceedings are turned into memes and are circulated in social media for profit, said Chaudhary.He complained there is no mechanism against these sinister designs aimed at diminishing public faith in the institution and judges by showing them in poor light.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant's 'cockroach' remark sparked a storm and gave birth to Cockroach Janta Party that led a Gen Z protest against NEET-UG paper leak. Supreme Court sought responses from govt and CBI on a PIL seeking action against those who commercially exploited the remark.

Article Title: Tiny plastic pan masala sachets may soon be history
Article Text:
Pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials (Photo: Agencies).

The rules came into force upon their publication in the gazette

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The tiny plastic sachet that has become synonymous with pan masala may finally be on its way out. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has notified plastic-free packaging norms for the product, a move experts say could further enforcement of an existing ban by allowing the food regulator to act directly against violators.The amended Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2026, require pan masala to be packed only in paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived materials free from plastic, or in tin or glass containers. The notification prohibits use of materials containing polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, PVC, synthetic polymers, laminates, aluminium foil and metallised layers, and also makes the packaging subject to Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.A senior FSSAI official told TOI that pan masala has been specifically included under Schedule IV of packaging regulations to provide Food Business Operators with clear guidance on suitable packaging materials, given the widespread use of small single-use packs and the environmental concerns arising from their disposal. However, environmental experts said the notification primarily furthers enforcement rather than imposing fresh prohibition.“The Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, had already placed an explicit legal ban on plastic sachets for gutka, tobacco and pan masala. The FSSAI notification reinforces that mandate through food safety regulations,” said Siddharth G. Singh, programme manager, solid waste management and circular economy, Centre for Science and Environment.He said enforcement of Plastic Waste Management Rules has remained patchy because it largely depends on state pollution control boards and local bodies. Bringing the requirement under the ambit of food safety regulations will allow FSSAI to act directly against Food Business Operators, plugging an enforcement gap that environmental laws alone struggled to address, he said.Singh said pan masala was specifically targeted because the sector relies heavily on use of small single-use sachets, which have a high littering potential and among the lowest collection rates.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has notified plastic- free packaging norms for the product. The move could further enforcement of an existing ban by allowing the food regulator to act directly against violators. The notification prohibits use of materials containing polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, PVC, synthetic polymers, laminates, aluminium foil and metallised layers.

Article Title: Benchmark hospital room cost against 3-star hotel tariff: Panel
Article Text:
Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison.

Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A patient’s hospital room in a private hospital could soon cost no more than a room in a nearby three-star hotel if a key recommendation of the parliamentary standing committee on health and family welfare is accepted. In an effort to rein in soaring medical bills, the panel has proposed linking room rents in private hospitals in major metropolitan cities to the average tariff charged by three-star hotels nearby.The recommendation is part of the committee’s report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector, which says the absence of a transparent mechanism for fixing room charges has led to wide variations in bills. It recommended benchmarking room rents to nearby three-star hotels, while allowing hospitals to levy separate charges for resident doctors, nursing care, consumables, meals and laundry.Citing the 80th National Sample Survey (Jan-Dec 2025), the panel said average cost of hospitalisation was Rs 6,631 in govt hospitals compared with Rs 50,508 in private hospitals. For childbirth alone, the average out-of-pocket expenditure was Rs 37,630 in private hospitals against Rs 2,299 in govt facilities.Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison. “Hotel room tariffs should not be the yardstick for hospital room rents because medical infra, staffing and support services are different,” said Dr Vinoy Kumar Upadhyay, CMD of Hope Hospital in Greater Noida.Noting the sharp difference in treatment costs, the panel said reducing out-of-pocket expenditure should be a key priority. It called for a legal mechanism to standardise and cap charges for essential treatments and routine procedures in private hospitals, mandatory disclosure of treatment costs before admission, and a fast-track grievance redressal mechanism for complaints related to billing.Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures. It also recommended advance cost estimates for complex treatments, financial navigators to guide patients on treatment costs and insurance, and ‘Continuum of Care’ packages covering screening, treatment and palliative care under a single capped payment. It urged the Centre to raise public health spending to 2.5% of GDP, strengthen govt hospitals, expand affordable medicines, and ensure stricter implementation of the Clinical Establishments Act.
Article Summary: The recommendation is part of the committee’s report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector. It recommended benchmarking room rents to nearby three-star hotels, while allowing hospitals to levy separate charges. Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison.

Article Title: States ignore Supreme Court, differ on NEET-PG seat norms
Article Text:
In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement

. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than a year after Supreme Court ruled that residence or domicile cannot be the basis for postgraduate medical admissions under the state quota, parents of NEET-PG aspirants say admission rules still vary across states, leaving students with unequal opportunities despite having taken the same national entrance examination.The concerns stem from SC’s Jan 29, 2025, judgement in Dr Tanvi Behl vs Shrey Goel case, which held that residence-based preference in postgraduate medical admissions is not permissible. The court said admissions should be based on NEET-PG scores while allowing only limited institutional preference, meaning a student may receive preference for having graduated from a particular medical college – and not because he or she is a resident or domicile of a state.The dispute primarily concerns private medical colleges, where admissions are conducted through state counselling. Several states prescribe domicile or other state-specific eligibility conditions. “The intention of the SC judgement was to replace residence-based preference with institutional preference. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.If these policies are challenged, the courts will decide whether they are consistent with the judgement. The Centre can still review the issue and issue uniform guidelines to states,” a health ministry official said.State counselling brochures for the NEET-PG admission process, reviewed by TOI, indeed show differences in eligibility rules. Gujarat requires additional state-specific eligibility conditions for some candidates who completed MBBS outside the state. Maharashtra allows only certain Maharashtra domicile candidates who studied outside the state to apply, while Karnataka permits candidates from other states to participate in counselling, though without Karnataka reservation benefits.Parents say these differences mean students with the same NEET-PG score may not have equal opportunity to compete for PG seats.In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement, a common national counselling portal and biannual NEET-PG examinations, arguing that students continue to face unequal admission opportunities across states. PMO has acknowledged the grievance, but no final decision has been communicated.Parents say the system also increases costs as candidates must register separately for multiple counselling processes, each with its own eligibility rules, timelines and security deposits. In response to one representation, NMC said domicile or residence-based reservation under state quota falls within the states’ jurisdiction and advised the complainant to approach the state or UT concerned. A similar representation to PMO in 2022 seeking uniform rules was closed after noting the concerns.
Article Summary: Parents of NEET-PG aspirants say admission rules still vary across states. Concerns stem from SC’s Jan 29, 2025, judgement in Dr Tanvi Behl vs Shrey Goel case. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.

Article Title: Old allies, new equation? Why SAD and BJP may join hands for 2027 Punjab assembly elections
Article Text:
BJP-SAD alliance buzz grows after PM Modi-Badal meeting

SAD's electoral decline

BJP-SAD alliance lasted nearly two decades before the parties split over the farm laws in 2020

Badal's changed tune on delimitation

'Why so desperate for BJP alliance?'

Why SAD alliance can help BJP

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BJP's bid to dominate?

NEW DELHI: Will the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal revive their decades-old ties in Punjab for the 2027 assembly elections? Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini, who has been playing a key role in BJP’s Punjab plans, has ruled out any such possibility. His denial comes amid a strong alliance buzz triggered by a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal last week - the first such meeting after the two parties snapped ties 6 years ago over the 3 farm bills.BJP’s Saini has played down alliance rumours. When asked to comment on the meeting, Saini replied in Punjabi, "Nahi, aise koyi gall nahi hai (No, there is no such thing)". The Haryana chief minister said the Prime Minister is the voice of 140 crore people. "If anyone wants to meet him, his doors are open; anyone can meet. Political parties keep meeting him for various issues."Saini further added, "Bharatiya Janata Party ka gathbandhan Punjab di janta de naal hai. (BJP's alliance is with the people of Punjab). And I say this with great confidence because I meet people there. In Punjab, the BJP is forming its government."So, can Saini’s denial be taken at face value? Or is it just political rhetoric to keep pressure on a regional party which appears desperate for an alliance with the BJP?Sukhbir Singh Badal, who has served two terms as deputy chief minister of Punjab and whose father Parkash Singh Badal was a 5-time chief minister, has been struggling to make a political comeback in the state. In the last two assembly elections, his party, SAD, has been pushed to the margins.The decline began in the 2017 assembly elections, when the SAD won only 15 of the 94 seats it contested, with a vote share of 25.24%. This was a sharp decline compared to its 2012 performance when the SAD had won 56 seats with a vote share of 34.73%. If 2017 was a worry, 2022, after it snapped ties with the BJP and contested alone, was a clear warning: the SAD could win only 3 seats, and its vote share dipped to 18.38%.This decline was not limited to just assembly elections. In the Lok Sabha elections too, SAD suffered a decline. In 2019, the SAD polled 27.76% of votes and won 2 seats. Five years later, while the seat reduced to 1, the vote share dipped to 13.48%. In 2014, the SAD tally in Lok Sabha was 4 seats and a 26.37% vote share.Clearly, for Sukhbir Singh Badal, both the crisis and the test are real. And that perhaps explains his visible desperation for an alliance with the BJP. And while the saffron party may reject alliance rumours, the SAD has sent clear signals of a strategic shift — extending a friendly hand to the BJP.In April this year, Badal had criticised the Centre’s move on delimitation of Lok Sabha seats in the garb of the Women’s Reservation Bill. "Punjab is predominantly a minority character state. We will be the biggest victim of this population-based delimitation. Compared with a nominal increase in seats for Punjab, Haryana will witness a nearly hundred per cent increase and double the number of its seats in the Lok Sabha," Badal had then said in a statement.Four months later, the SAD chief has literally taken a U-turn on the issue. After his meeting with PM Modi, Badal changed his stand and demanded the immediate implementation of the Women’s Reservation Bill. He also supported the Union government’s proposal to increase Parliament seats in states by 50 per cent.In a new statement after his meeting with PM Modi, Badal said the party stood for a fair and equitable delimitation exercise that ensured equal increase in representation to all states. “This will ensure justice is done to all states,” he said.Badal’s changed stand prompted a dig from Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who asked the Shiromani Akali Dal chief as to why he was so desperate for an electoral alliance with the BJP that he had to make a U-turn on a sensitive matter like delimitation of the assembly and parliamentary constituencies.“What changed within these months that you started seeing merit in the same Bill, you otherwise found against Punjab’s interests?” he asked. “Sukhbir has turned more loyal than the king within no time,” Warring said.He said when the Akalis had failed to reach an alliance with the BJP ahead of the parliamentary elections, Badal had claimed that he did not want to compromise on the interests of Punjab. “Now that you are desperate for your own survival, you have simply forgotten the interests of Punjab for which you claimed to have taken a stand in 2024,” said Warring.Chief minister Bhagwant Mann also took potshots at Badal and said, "BJP can make them do whatever they want. SAD just wants to get back into the cabinet in Delhi or get into an alliance with the BJP in Punjab."These reactions would suggest that both the ruling AAP and the Congress are perhaps aware how a potential BJP-Akali alliance could change the dynamics on ground. While they may play down the possible impact of this alliance, they would be keeping a close eye on the developments. AAP would hope that the 2027 Punjab contest stays four-cornered so that the ruling party can benefit from the division of opposition votes. The Congress, on the other hand, realises that SAD could help the BJP in rural areas and add to the party's challenges in the state.Little wonder, Badal would not mind their political barbs as long as he can secure the future of his party with the BJP. And that brings us to Saini’s remark playing down the meeting between PM Modi and Sukhbir Badal.For the BJP, the Akali association is electorally important, at least for now. The BJP has just two seats in the current assembly with a vote share of 6.6%. The party could not win a single seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections despite polling 18.65% of votes. This was almost double of the 9.74% that the BJP managed in 2019 Lok Sabha elections. It was also a huge jump from the 2022 assembly elections when the BJP got just 6.6% of votes. But the fact that BJP could win 2 Lok Sabha seats in 2019 despite a low vote share points to the importance of SAD alliance in converting votes to seats in the state.Despite the sharp decline in its electoral fortunes, the Shiromani Akali Dal still has good support base in rural Punjab and also has a strong Sikh-centric regional identity - both of which can help the BJP in case of an alliance. Combined with BJP's urban support base, this can turn into a winning combination for the two parties. The SAD has been going all out to increase its base and presence in the state.The controversy around movie Satluj, which narrates the life story of activist Jaswant Singh Khalra - who uncovered alleged extrajudicial cremations in Punjab between mid-1980s and early-1990s, gave SAD the much-needed boost to woo its core voters. When the movie was taken down from the OTT platform, SAD arranged its screening across Punjab. In a post on X in Punjabi, Badal had then said, "In every village and corner of Punjab, the SAD will screen the film 'Satluj' based on inhuman atrocities inflicted on thousands of innocent Sikh youth and Sikh personalities like Shaheed Bhai Jaswant Singh Ji Khalra during the Congress regime, so that our children and future generations can be thoroughly acquainted with the oppression inflicted. "Badal had justified the move and said:"This is aimed at ensuring that today's youth and our coming generations know about the unspeakable tragedy and repression unleashed by the then Congress governments against Bhai Jaswant Singh Khalra and thousands of other innocent Sikh youth who were eliminated through fake encounters." The aggressive SAD campaign was clearly a move to consolidate its ‘Panthic’ vote bank - a political mobilisation surrounding the Sikh community’s collective identity.The SAD perhaps can complement the BJP if the two parties eventually agree for an alliance.Hence, the BJP’s posturing vis-a-vis the SAD alliance at present perhaps has more to do with asserting who will dictate terms if and when the two parties join hands. And this is important as till 2020, when the partnership snapped, the SAD was the senior partner in Punjab’s NDA alliance and the BJP played second fiddle. That political dynamic has changed now. By repeatedly asserting that it will contest the Punjab elections on its own, the BJP has clearly spread the message that it will lead the fight and not play the junior partner to anyone. Hence, the saffron party would not want to miss any opportunity to reinforce this message to the SAD leadership and its cadres.True, the BJP is working on a roadmap to increase its political base and strength and become an independent political force in Punjab. This is manifested in the several steps that the party has taken in Punjab. From Prime Minister’s Punjab rallies to party chief Nitin Nabin’s push and targeted acquisition from political rivals, the BJP has made it clear that it means business in Punjab. But the party perhaps will need more time to do a Bengal in Punjab, if at all it ever happens. For now, SAD perhaps could be its best bet in Punjab.
Article Summary: BJP-SAD alliance lasted nearly two decades before the parties split over the farm laws in 2020. Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini, who has been playing a key role in BJP’s Punjab plans, has ruled out any such possibility.

Article Title: ‘Only God can save this country’: HC bins plea of J&K cop sacked for skipping duty over terror threat
Article Text:
"Engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,” the HC noted.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Srinagar: Only God can save this country if a police officer, of whatever rank, gets frightened by terrorists’ threats and refuses duties, J&K high court has said while dismissing a cop’s petition for reinstatement.“The justification provided by the petitioner for not attending his duties is unacceptable, to say the least,” a single bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar said in its Monday order. The judge rejected special police officer (SPO) Hemo Hamid Wani’s argument that he was entitled to the “same powers, privileges and protections available to ordinary officers of police under Police Act”. The HC pointed out that “SPOs do not hold any civil posts regulated by statutory rules”.Residents of a neighbourhood are appointed SPOs “for specific purposes when the force ordinarily employed for preserving peace is not sufficient”. “Thus, engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,” the HC noted.Wani was engaged as an SPO in 2012. In 2015, he was posted at Reshipora in south Kashmir’s Shopian. While at home on medical leave at one point then, he received life threats from terrorists and failed to report back to duties.When he returned after some time to his posting, he was not allowed to join duty, forcing him to take the matter to senior officers.When no action was taken, Wani moved the HC. In Aug last year, the court directed the J&K police DGP to take a decision on Wani’s plea. The DGP turned it down, forcing Wani to move the HC again.In his HC petition, Wani argued that J&K Police had disengaged him without inquiry, formal charges or hearing. The action, he said, violated the Constitution’s Articles 16 (equality of opportunity in public employment), 21 (right to life and livelihood) and 311 (protection against arbitrary dismissal), besides provisions of J&K Police Rules.The HC rejected the contentions, saying Wani, as an SPO, was not entitled to any hearing or inquiry in view of the temporary nature of his engagement. Even if it is assumed that Wani had the right to such a hearing, his failure to perform duties in the face of terror threats is enough reason to remove him, the HC held.“Granting an opportunity to the petitioner to present his case prior to disengagement would have been an empty formality. The DGP has rightly rejected the petitioner’s representation. The order does not call for any interference,” Justice Dhar observed.
Article Summary: J&K high court dismisses a cop's petition for reinstatement. Hemo Hamid Wani was engaged as an SPO in 2012. In 2015, he was posted at Reshipora in south Kashmir’s Shopian. While at home on medical leave, he received life threats from terrorists.

Article Title: Air India Phuket flight probe: Marijuana’s legal availability adds to worries of airlines
Article Text:
Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. The reason: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members, say officials across multiple airlines, is to increase random dope testing, as there substances usually remain present in the body for much longer than alcohol.The concern across airlines globally to check this stems from the fact that operating a flight “under the influence of any psychoactive substance might render (licensed personnel like pilots) unable to safely and properly exercise” perform their duty, as per the International Civil Aviation Organisation.Possibly the most infamous case of this was a US carrier’s off-duty pilot travelling on the jump seat (extra seat behind pilots) in the flight deck trying to shut down the engines. This off-duty pilot had reportedly taken psychedelic mushrooms two days before the incident and hadn’t slept in 48 hours. “This is a challenge globally. Often the tests are not conclusive if taking some medicine leads to detection of psychoactive substances.However, recent consumption of drugs does show up in tests,” said officials.DGCA rules on “procedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances” says: “In case the confirmatory test is found positive, the medical in charge of the organisation shall consult a medical review officer to determine if the result was due to a legitimate therapeutic treatment or some other innocuous source (for example pain relief medication containing codeine may trigger a positive result for opiates).Airlines try to create awareness and encourage employees to anonymously report addiction so that the same can be addressed. But mostly people avoid reporting the same, so this virtually remains a non-starter, said many officials. Officials running operations across airlines say the focus in India is primarily on self-reporting and de-addiction.“But given the easy availability of psychoactive substances, we need to make the consequences a bit tougher and act as deterrent. We have to increase random testing, that’s the only way out,” said an official. Under DGCA rules, all scheduled commercial airlines and air navigation service providers need to test at least 10% of their flight crew members and air traffic controllers every year.
Article Summary: The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members is to increase random dope testing.

Article Title: The road not taken, every day: Why do potholes keep coming back
Article Text:
Pothole-related deaths in India rose by over 53% in five years, from 1,555 in 2020 to 2,385 in 2024.

From a tiny crack to a full-blown pothole, here's how road damage turns into a recurring cycle of patch and repair.

Every pothole starts small

A police officer fills a pothole with stones on a road, at Edappally, in Kochi. (Image credit: PTI)

Why does the pothole come back after it is fixed

Potholes on Bengaluru roads (Image credit: PTI)

What data shows

Can we stop pothole before it becomes a pothole?

How speed, rain, poor visibility and heavy traffic can turn a road defect into a serious hazard.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Do you also have a “work in progress” sign permanently living outside your house?One day, someone digs up the road to lay a water pipe. A few days later, another team arrives to fix a cable. Then comes the patchwork. And just when you think the road is finally back to normal, congratulations, it is dug up again.The road outside your house may technically be the same road, but it has seen so many rounds of digging, filling, breaking and repairing that it almost has a career history.And then, inevitably, the potholes arrive.We often blame potholes on bad roads, heavy rain or poor construction. But a pothole is rarely born overnight. In fact, that annoying crater that makes your car suspension groan or sends a two-wheeler rider swerving usually has a long backstory.A crack appears. Water gets in. The road weakens. Traffic keeps pounding it. The surface finally gives way.And if the underlying problem isn't fixed, filling the hole may only be a temporary solution.The road gets dug up. Again. And again.Before we get to the pothole itself, there is another character in this story: road digging.Roads don't just carry vehicles. They carry water pipelines, sewage lines, electricity cables, telecom networks and other utilities underneath them. Whenever something needs to be repaired, replaced or newly installed, the road may have to be opened.The problem begins when the road is not restored to the same standard after the work is completed.A poorly compacted patch can become weaker than the surrounding pavement. Water can seep into the edges. Traffic repeatedly hits the repaired section. Eventually, cracks appear.And suddenly, the “temporary” patch becomes the next pothole.This is one reason why road maintenance cannot simply mean filling visible holes. What happens underneath the road matters just as much as what you see on top.The first warning sign is usually something you wouldn't give a second glance: a tiny crack.Road surfaces are constantly under pressure. India's roads have to handle enormous traffic volumes, heavy vehicles and, in many parts of the country, intense heat followed by heavy monsoon rain.Temperature changes cause pavement materials to expand and contract. Repeated traffic loads create fatigue. Overloaded vehicles put additional stress on the surface.Then the monsoon arrives.That tiny crack suddenly becomes a doorway.Water is the real troublemakerRain itself isn't necessarily the villain. Water getting beneath the road is.Once water enters through a crack, it can reach the layers beneath the asphalt. If drainage is poor, clogged or badly designed, the water may remain there instead of being carried away.The result is gradual weakening of the road's foundation.The surface may still look fine from above. Underneath, however, the supporting layers can lose strength and material can be washed or displaced, creating weak spots and voids.And then traffic does what traffic does best: keeps coming.Then the tyres take overImagine standing on a floor that has suddenly become slightly hollow underneath. Now imagine thousands of vehicles repeatedly pressing down on that same spot.That is essentially what happens to a road whose underlying layers have weakened.With every passing vehicle, the damaged surface experiences another load. Bits of asphalt loosen, the depression grows and eventually the surface collapses.That is your pothole.And once it forms, it can become a vicious cycle.Rainwater collects in the depression. More water finds its way into the surrounding pavement. The edges weaken. Vehicles hit the damaged section. More material breaks away.A small pothole can therefore become a much bigger one surprisingly quickly, especially during the rainy season.Now comes the question every commuter has asked at least once:“Didn't they just repair this?”Yes. But repairing the hole and repairing the road are not always the same thing.If workers simply fill the visible depression while the layers underneath remain damaged, the surface may fail again.It is a bit like filling a dent in a wall without fixing the leak behind it.The road may look perfect for a while. Then water gets in again, traffic starts pounding the weak section and — hello, pothole.This is why preventive maintenance matters. A small crack can often be dealt with before it becomes structural damage. Once the road base itself has deteriorated, the repair becomes more complicated, expensive and disruptive.And not all potholes are equally dangerousA pothole's danger isn't determined by its size alone.A small hole on a busy, high-speed road can be far more dangerous than a giant one on an empty lane.For two-wheelers, an unexpected depression can destabilise the vehicle. On a crowded road, a driver trying to avoid a pothole may suddenly brake or swerve. At night, poor lighting can make the defect difficult to spot. During rain, water can completely hide its depth.So the real danger is a combination of the pothole, speed, traffic, visibility and road conditions.Potholes claimed 9,438 lives across India between 2020 and 2024, with annual fatalities rising from 1,555 in 2020 to 2,385 in 2024 — a jump of more than 53% in five years. Uttar Pradesh accounted for more than half of the national toll, reporting 5,127 deaths. Madhya Pradesh followed with 969 fatalities, while Tamil Nadu recorded 612, Odisha 425, Punjab 414 and Assam 395. Among Union Territories, Delhi reported the highest toll at 50.But the numbers also raise questions about how pothole-related crashes are recorded. States such as Andhra Pradesh and Bihar reported zero crashes, injuries or deaths under this category, even as states such as Manipur, Nagaland and Tripura reported fatalities. Experts say gaps in objective crash-cause reporting could mean the data does not fully capture the scale of the problem.The toll, however, remains below the 2017 peak of 3,597 pothole-related deaths. The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of the issue in 2018, observing that authorities responsible for maintaining roads were failing in their duties.Fortunately, the answer isn't simply “keep filling holes”.A 2021 IIT Madras study found that nearly 78% of urban potholes reported by citizens remained unfixed for more than two weeks, with delays particularly serious in high-traffic areas.Technology can help road agencies identify damage earlier through road-condition monitoring, GIS mapping and scanning systems. Quick repair methods can deal with certain defects before they expand.Citizen reporting can also help — provided complaints actually lead to inspection and action.Because the person who encounters a dangerous pothole may not be a road engineer inspecting the highway once a month. It may be a delivery rider passing through it ten times a day.But technology alone won't solve the problem.Road agencies need better coordination too. If one department digs up a road to lay a cable and another has to repair it later, someone needs to ensure the road is restored properly. Otherwise, the same stretch can enter an endless loop of dig → patch → crack → pothole → repair → dig again.The pothole is only the final chapterSo, the next time you see a pothole outside your home, remember: that hole probably didn't just “appear”.It may have started as a tiny crack.Then came rainwater. Maybe a badly repaired utility cut. Maybe years of heavy traffic. Maybe poor drainage. Maybe all of them.By the time you notice the crater, the real damage may already be underneath.Which is why the real solution isn't simply asking, “Who will fill this pothole?”It is asking a much more important question:“Why did this road fail in the first place — and why wasn't it fixed before it got this bad?”Because if the answer remains unclear, that freshly filled pothole may just be waiting for its next monsoon comeback.
Article Summary: Pothole-related deaths in India rose by over 53% in five years, from 1,555 in 2020 to 2,385 in 2024. From a tiny crack to a full-blown pothole, here's how road damage turns into a recurring cycle of patch and repair.

NEW DELHI: Over 9.69 crore person-days have been generated in approximately a month of the rollout of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-G RAM G) which replaced MGNREGA , the govt informed Lok Sabha on Tuesday.When VB- G RAM G Scheme was rolled out from July 1, revised wage rates were notified by the govt with a new interim base wage rate of Rs 300 per day. With this the national average notified wage increased from Rs 298.8 per day under MGNREGA to Rs 327.4 under VB–G RAM G, representing an average increase of Rs 28.6 per day. Prior to this notification, wage rates in several states were below Rs 300, with the lowest notified wage being Rs 241 per day.Meanwhile, the parliamentary standing committee on rural development and panchayati raj in its report submitted in Parliament on Tuesday recommended a comprehensive review of the wage-determination methodology including the appropriateness of the 2011 base year and the adequacy of CPI-AL and consider instituting a minimum wage floor of Rs 400 per day with regional differentiation and ensure systematic and meaningful indexation to a robust inflation indicator that reflects actual rural living costs.“Pending structural revision, necessary fiscal space should be sought for a significant upward adjustment in the current cycle,” the panel chaired by Congress MP Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka recommended. The Committee in its report, on the action taken on the recommendations contained in its earlier report submitted in Parliament in March on 'Demands for Grants (2026-27) related to the department of rural development, has sought an action taken report on the fresh recommendations within three months.In a written response to a question asked by Congress MPs Vijayakumar Alias Vijay Vasanth and Manickam Tagore, rural development minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan informed the Lok Sabha that the VB-G RAM G scheme has been implemented in rural areas of the entire country.The VB-G RAM G scheme provides for a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work against 100 days of guaranteed wage employment available under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS.In response to the question on whether the govt has taken note of concerns raised by several State Governments regarding the financial structure of VB-G RAM-G and details of the reasons for shifting financial burden to states up to 40% under VB-G RAM-G. “Presently almost all centrally sponsored schemes (CSS) across sectors are being implemented on the 60:40 sharing model. The 60:40 pattern adopted under this Act is therefore consistent with the broader framework of Centrally Sponsored Schemes,” the minister said and shared that regular consultations were being held with states. The fund sharing pattern is 90:10 with the Centre bearing 90% of the expenditure incase of union territories and northeastern and Himalayan states.
Article Summary: Over 9.69 crore person-days have been generated in approximately a month of the rollout of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-G RAM G) which replaced MGNREGA. Article Title: Shield people from unlawful digital content, SC tells govt
Article Text:
