NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Union ministries of home affairs and electronics and information technology to take urgent steps to create a URL-specific and judicially supervised emergency mechanism to protect citizens from grave unlawful digital content.While disposing of a PIL by advocate N K Goswami, a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant said the petitioner in public interest had highlighted the danger from digital threats of violence, doxxing, exposure of minor children’s private details, non-consensual intimate/deepfake content and identity-manipulating digital impersonation.The SC bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said such cyber crimes severely impacted an individual’s right to freedom of speech, the right to dignity, privacy and the right to life.It said the petitioner had highlighted protections against such threats using internet, digital mediums and Artificial Intelligence existing in other countries and suggested to the govt to consider problems highlighted in PIL for urgent remedial measures.Goswami said given the misuse of AI and proliferation of social media and its reach, it was urgently required to create “a constitutionally compliant emergency mechanism against grave unlawful digital harms, namely specific threats, doxxing, unauthorised exposure of children’s private details, non-consensual intimate or Al-generated morphed content, and deepfake/digitally manipulated impersonation causing immediate grave harm”.He said he neither sought a blanket ban on any speech nor suppression of political speech, criticism, satire, parody, journalism, academic comment, public-interest reporting, or legal commentary.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asks Union ministries of home affairs and electronics and information technology to take urgent steps to protect citizens from grave unlawful digital content. NEW DELHI: Tribunal Reforms Bill, piloted by govt in Parliament, is seen as a move that reinforces the constitutional position in appointments: ensuring primacy of the judiciary in deciding top positions. At the same time, it seeks to maintain a three-tier architecture between the tribunal, the secretariat and the administrative ministry with clear roles mapped out for each.In the bill — passed by RS Tuesday and LS Monday — govt has sought to ensure the independence of National Tribunals Commission (NTC) that will supervise the appointment, functioning, discipline and administrative needs of tribunals. To be headed by a retired judge of the Supreme Court or chief justice of a high court, the proposed NTC will have two judicial members drawn from among retired HC judges apart from two technical members. The chairperson and judicial members will be appointed by govt in consultation with the CJI.The commission, through its search and selection committee, has been tasked to streamline selection of chairpersons and members of tribunals. Unlike the current system, where a panel of names is sent, the committee will recommend a single name for each vacancy, along with a waiting list. Strict timelines have been proposed for recommending names to govt and for the Centre to approve them.It addresses a constant complaint that ministries have in appointments getting delayed.Besides, govt has decided to fix the retirement age of chairperson of tribunals at 70 years, with members to retire at 67, unless they complete their five-year terms.The commission will be assisted by a secretariat with the administrative ministry having no role in either advertising for the post or scrutinising the candidates. The ministry concerned will merely forward inputs to the secretariat on the candidate and Intelligence Bureau will provide its reports. Officials argued that this will end any possible conflict of interest that the ministry concerned will have as a litigant.
Article Summary: Tribunal Reforms Bill, piloted by govt in Parliament, is seen as a move that reinforces the constitutional position in appointments. It seeks to maintain a three-tier architecture between the tribunal, the secretariat and the administrative ministry with clear roles mapped out for each.

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh is indisputably an integral and inalienable part of India, govt asserted Tuesday in response to Beijing’s rejection of its decision to formally identify and map 27 places in the state. Following recent reports about fresh border tensions, govt also reiterated that “the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of larger bilateral ties”.The home ministry had last week identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by “standard place and feature names” on the official maps of Survey of India, saying this would facilitate their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public. China, which has at least on six occasions assigned new names to places in Arunachal to reinforce its claim over the state, called the action “illegal, null and void”.“Arunachal Pradesh is an integral and inalienable part of India, and this is a self-evident fact. Nothing can change this indisputable reality,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, responding to queries about remarks by the Chinese foreign ministry.The Indian exercise had followed unconfirmed reports of incursions by PLA into Arunachal Pradesh. CM Pema Khandu had denied there was any such incursion by Chinese troops.The MEA said India had always emphasised that the maintenance of peace in border areas was of the utmost importance. “We have also stated that the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties,” Jaiswal said, adding this was reiterated at the 36th Meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China border affairs, where the two sides engaged in “frank discussions” and reviewed the situation along LAC.“It was agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels... to avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along LAC,” the official said.

NEW DELHI: After being at the receiving end of the opposition’s protest for days, NDA MPs went on the offensive Tuesday as they seized on police action against protesting students in Jharkhand to stage a march in Parliament complex targeting Rahul Gandhi, with former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan calling him a habitual liar who “neither wants to come to Parliament nor listen to answers”.As the governing alliance accused Rahul of “running away” from a discussion after govt agreed to his demand for home minister Amit Shah’s statement on the alleged use of excessive force regarding students’ interests, but crushing the country’s and youth’s interests by obstructing Parliament proceedings.Both sides came face to face near Makar Dwar, the main entrance to Parliament, prompting security staff to build a cordon around them.It was not without some moments of amusement, however, as Congress MP Pawan Khera was seen attacking govt in comments to the media, while MPs from BJP and its allies around him with placards against Rahul.From the venue of their parliamentary party meeting, NDA MPs carried a big banner, taunting Rahul for “running away” from govt’s offer to discuss the student protest in Delhi and Shah’s reply.The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha had rejected govt’s proposal, saying all three of their demands, including PM Narendra Modi’s statement on donation theft issue, were non-negotiable.With Rahul criticising the use of force against students in Jharkhand, BJP dared him to withdraw his party’s support to the state govt headed by JMM’s Hemant Soren.Students in Jharkhand, where the JMM-Congress alliance is in office, were baton-charged by police and many of them were injured, but no one has resigned from state govt, BJP MP Anurag Thakur said. “When the home minister is ready to reply in Parliament, Rahul does not want to come. Congress is using students for its politics,” he said.Opposition MPs protested the Ram temple donation theft and alleged police excesses in Delhi on July 20. Congress’s Priyanka Gandhi Vadra claimed the opposition had forced even governing alliance MPs to protest, adding govt should now make a statement. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said the theft and police action were linked to the same organisation, taking a swipe at RSS.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said govt had gone beyond Rahul’s demand for a statement from Shah by agreeing to a debate but he was now running away.Shiv Sena’s Shrikant Shinde and RLM’s Upendra Kushwaha said the opposition was determined to disrupt Parliament under one pretext or another. Rahul is engaging in selective outrage, Shinde said.
Article Summary: NDA MPs seized on police action against protesting students in Jharkhand to stage a march in Parliament complex targeting Rahul Gandhi. Former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan called him a habitual liar who “neither wants to come to Parliament nor listen to answers”

JAMMU: Security forces launched joint cordon-and-search operations in J&K’s Doda and Poonch districts on being alerted about the sighting of terror suspects, officials said Tuesday.Cordon-and-search operations were initiated in Doda’s upper reaches after some locals captured a video of four suspected ultras trekking along Ramtund Peak and informed authorities late Monday afternoon. According to preliminary information, the group allegedly comprised three Pakistani and one local terrorist.Additional personnel from the Army, CRPF and police, along with reinforcements, were rushed to the area from Udhampur on Tuesday morning, officials said, adding that no contact was established with the suspects until evening.Ramtund area lies near the Seoj Dhar belt, situated on the Doda-Udhampur axis, which further connects to Kathua region. Terrorists have traditionally used this route to travel and hide, as the topography features dense vegetation and natural caves, officials said.The searches in Doda came four days after local police put up posters across J&K, announcing Rs 15 lakh reward for credible information leading to the arrest of self-styled Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat.Separately, security forces launched an intensive combing operation in Poonch’s Mendhar sector upon noticing suspicious movement near an under-construction tunnel. “A security guard manning the site spotted the suspects and fired three to four rounds as a precautionary measure, following which a joint team of SOG and CRPF launched a search operation around 6am Tuesday in the nearby forested stretches of Bhatadurian, Sangiot and adjoining areas,” an official said.
